title: The photo-app numbers, turned into boxes
caption: 23 writes/s, 17k peak reads/s, 5.5 PB and 23 Gbps each pick a different component.

steps.text: Egress ≈ 23 Gbps (5 800 reads/s × 500 KB × 8). The CDN serves photo bytes from the edge and only goes to the origin on a miss.
Peak ≈ 17 400 metadata reads/s: too much for one database, easy for a few stateless API servers behind a load balancer.
Read:write ≈ 250:1, so optimise the read path: a cache holds hot metadata, and the DB (plus read replicas) serves misses. 23 writes/s is trivial for one primary.
Storage ≈ 5 475 TB over 5 years with 3 replicas: that is object storage, never database rows. Metadata is ~1 KB per photo, about 2 GB/day.

scenarios.name: 10× traffic
scenarios.summary: Multiply every number by 10 and re-ask which box breaks: the read path and egress need more nodes, while writes still fit one primary.

steps.text: 100 M users instead of 10 M: peak metadata reads ≈ 174 000/s. Stateless API servers just scale out behind the LB.
One cache node (~100k ops/s) is no longer enough: shard the cache across several nodes by photo id.
Writes ≈ 230/s: still easy for one primary. The DB doesn't need sharding for writes, only for its growing size.
Egress ≈ 230 Gbps and storage ≈ 55 PB: the CDN hit ratio and object storage now carry the design (and the bill).

scenarios.name: Alternative: no cache
scenarios.summary: Serve metadata reads from read replicas instead of a cache: one fewer technology, but ~4 more DB machines, replica lag and millisecond reads.

steps.text: Writes (23/s) go to the primary, exactly as before.
17 400 peak reads/s ÷ ~5 000 per replica ≈ 4 read replicas.
Trade-off: no cache to keep in sync, but more database machines, each read costs ms instead of µs, and replicas can lag a write by a second.
Worth it when reads have a low hit rate (every user reads different data) and a cache would mostly miss.

scenarios.name: Risk: the egress bill
scenarios.summary: 23 Gbps is ~250 TB a day: if the CDN misses, the origin can't keep up and the transfer bill runs to thousands of dollars a day.

steps.text: 23 Gbps ≈ 2.9 GB/s ≈ 250 TB per day leaving your system. At a few cents per GB that's on the order of $10 000 a day.
A cold or purged CDN (new region, cache flush, a viral photo) sends misses to the origin, which was sized for a trickle.
Mitigation: serve resized variants (a 100 KB thumbnail instead of 500 KB is 5× less), keep the hit ratio high and add an origin shield tier.
